brief: A calendar showing energy levels — mornings are high ground, post-lunch dips are valleys

dominant_strengths: Clear calendar grid with consistent spacing and a legible weekday header that anchors the dense data visualization beneath it.
Six-tier energy legend maps directly to colored bars per day, creating a recognizable system for scanning weekly rhythms.
Selected day (13) uses a subtle tint and percentage callout, showing thoughtful state differentiation amid a noisy grid.
dominant_weaknesses: Every cell shows 4-5 stacked bars with no clear hierarchy — viewer cannot tell which value is 'today's energy' vs reference.
Six similar greens plus orange/red/yellow create chromatic overload; legend categories blur visually and undermine the brief's morning-vs-valley narrative.
Bars are decorative not quantitative — no axis, no time-of-day labels, so the 'morning high / afternoon valley' story is invisible to users.
fix_priorities: Replace stacked bars with a single sparkline or area curve per day showing energy across hours, making valleys literally visible.
Collapse legend to 3-4 tiers (Peak/Moderate/Low/Rest) and reduce green proximity to restore color discrimination.
Add micro time-axis labels (AM/PM) on hover or selected day, so the brief's circadian framing becomes legible.
Strengthen selected-day treatment with stronger contrast and contextual detail panel rather than just a faint background.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral color-richness outpaces behavioral clarity, and reflective insight is weak because the chart can't be decoded into a daily narrative.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — it encodes energy categories but fails to express the morning-peak/post-lunch-valley shape the brief promises.
